stem.text: Let \( f(x) = xe^{-x/2} \) and \( g(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x - 1.5)^{2} \). The graphs of \( f \) and \( g \) intersect at exactly two points, where \( x = p \) and \( x = q \) with \( 0 < p < q \). Let \( R \) be the region bounded by the graphs of \( f \) and \( g \).

parts.prompt: Region \( R \) is the base of a solid whose cross sections perpendicular to the \( x \)-axis are squares. Find the volume of the solid.

worked_solution.text: Solve f(x) = g(x) on the calculator for the limits.
Each square has side f(x) - g(x), the vertical distance across R, so its area is the square of that distance.

points.criterion: Writes the definite integral of (f(x) - g(x))^2, in either order of subtraction, from x = p to x = q, with the limits written as p and q or as decimals about 0.573 and 2.684. An integrand with a factor of pi, or the area f(x) - g(x) unsquared, earns nothing.
Gives the volume 0.575, accurate to three decimal places.

parts.prompt: Region \( R \) is the base of a second solid whose cross sections perpendicular to the \( x \)-axis are semicircles with diameters lying in \( R \). Find the volume of this solid.

worked_solution.text: The diameter is f(x) - g(x), so the radius is half of it and the semicircle's area is one half pi times the radius squared.
Integrate from p to q and evaluate on the calculator.

points.criterion: Writes a definite integral from x = p to x = q (or the decimal limits) of the semicircle area (pi/8)(f(x) - g(x))^2, with the constant inside or in front of the integral, or in the form (pi/2)((f(x) - g(x))/2)^2. Using f(x) - g(x) as the radius, giving (pi/2)(f(x) - g(x))^2, earns nothing.
Gives the volume 0.226, accurate to three decimal places.

parts.prompt: Let \( S \) be the region bounded by the graph of \( f \), the \( x \)-axis, and the vertical line \( x = 2 \). Region \( S \) is the base of a solid whose cross sections perpendicular to the \( x \)-axis are squares. Write an integral expression for the volume of this solid, and use integration by parts to find the volume. Show the work that leads to your answer.

worked_solution.text: Each square has side f(x), so its area is f(x) squared.
Parts with u = x^2 and dv = e^{-x} dx, so du = 2x dx and v = -e^{-x}.
Parts again with u = 2x and dv = e^{-x} dx, so du = 2 dx and v = -e^{-x}.

points.criterion: Writes the definite integral of (f(x))^2, that is x^2 e^(-x), from x = 0 to x = 2.
Chooses u = x^2 and dv = e^(-x) dx with du = 2x dx and v = -e^(-x), stated or visible in the resulting expression. The choice u = e^(-x) with dv = x^2 dx earns nothing.
Writes the first parts expression -x^2 e^(-x) minus the integral of -2x e^(-x) dx, or an equivalent arrangement with the remaining integral present, with or without limits.

Applies parts a second time to the integral of 2x e^(-x) dx, writing -2x e^(-x) plus the integral of 2e^(-x) dx or an equivalent arrangement, and reaches an antiderivative equivalent to -(x^2 + 2x + 2)e^(-x). A tabular method that shows the same terms earns this point.
Gives the volume 2 - 10e^(-2), or an equivalent exact form, or the decimal 0.646 or 0.647.
